text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- U.N. administrator for eastern Salvonia Jacques Klein expects most Serbs to remain in the area after its reintegration in Croatia.
- German metal firm Krupp ready to continue cooperation with Yugoslav firms, most interested in cooperating in modernisation of Yugosalv railways.
- Sufficient quantities of seed, fertiliser and pesticide have been secured for spring sowing on some 2,3 million hectares says Predrag Dumanovic of the Yugoslav Chamber of Economy.

- Newly-appointed Serbian Information Minister Radmila Milentijevic says her task is to show the world the real truth about Yugoslavia to the best of her ability, to work more closely with foreign media in the country.

- Serb intellectual forum from Banja Luka addresses letter to International High Respresentative Carl Bildt asking for the decision under which Brcko inter-entity boundary line remains unchanged be declared final.
NASA BORBA
- Opposition coalition Zajedno stops protest marches while student protests continue in the streets of Belgrade.
- Opposition Democratic Party MP's will return to the federal parliament which they boycotted because of annullment of local election results.
- Teachers insist on continuing strike because the Serbian government offers them much less than they demand.
- Despite numerous strikes over outstanding wages there are no pressures on the central bank for printing money, says vice-governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia Ratko Banovic.
- Special U.N. human rights rapporteur Eisabeth Rehn makes short stop-over in Belgrade on her way to Croatia, meets opposition leader and students and strsses need for democracy.

- New Serbian finance minister Dragan Tomic to resign as president of Holding company Simpo because he cannot hold both posts under the law, the paper learns. The new company president expected to be his wife Edit Tomic.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Bosnian Serb parliament deputies dissatisfied with the Brcko arbitrage decision, believe it leaves room for Moslem provocations.

- Representatives of Serbian education trade union criticise return to school agreement signed by the government and Serbian and Belgrade trade unions without them, say it will bring great harm to education.
- Vranje tobacco industry faces bankruptcy if a halt is not put to illicit cigarette trade.

- Very high steel import quotas and large quantities of illegally imported steel have blocked the market and brought to a halt production in Montenegro's largest steel plant Zeljezara Niksic, warns plant director and president of Montenegrin chamber of Economy Vojin Djukanovic.
VECERNJE NOVOSIT
- Kolubara mining basin produces 2.4 million tonnes of coal in January, 20 percent above plan, 1997 productionexpected to reach 25 million tonnes.
-- Belgrade newsroom, 381 11 222 43 05
